title: An extended certificate of small size is decided by the matchings it forces
source_title: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings

standard_prerequisites.name: Extended certificate
standard_prerequisites.statement: A certificate together with one additional triple of indices, recording that a matching satisfies the pairs and the triple in a prescribed way.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object whose consequence is asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: Satisfying a certificate
standard_prerequisites.statement: A perfect matching satisfies a certificate when it contains all its pairs, and it satisfies an extended one when in addition the triple is arranged as prescribed.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation between the two hypotheses of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pair representation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A matching satisfying a small certificate consists of that certificate together with several further pairs, which leaves enough room for two flips.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the bound that guarantees the two alternative matchings exist.

core_obligations: Assume a matching satisfies the pairs of the extended certificate but not its triple, and normalise so that the offending pair is the one joining the first two indices of the triple (source line 698).

Use the size bound to find two further pairs and build the two flips of the matching obtained by replacing those pairs with the crossed pairings, both of which avoid all three pairs of the triple (source lines 700-704).
Check that in either case a matching containing one of the crossed pairs cannot contain the others, so the prescribed triple is forced, and conclude (source line 705).

proof_roadmap.step: Normalise the offending pair and count the remaining pairs.
Build the two flips of the matching.
Rule out the alternatives and conclude the triple is forced.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 694-696: for an extended certificate of size at most n minus two and a second certificate of the same size, if two matchings are related in the prescribed way and one of them fails the triple of the extended certificate while satisfying its pairs, then the other fails a specific pair of the second certificate. The proof (source lines 697-706) is a flip argument: the failing matching is normalised so that the offending pair joins the first two indices of the triple, the size bound guarantees at least three further pairs so that two alternative matchings can be built by crossing two pairs at a time, both alternatives avoid the three pairs of the triple, and the exclusion of the remaining possibilities forces the prescribed triple. The statement records the implication and none of the flipping.
